extra.message: The unauthenticated pastes resolver interpolates the client-controlled filter argument into SQLAlchemy text(): "title = '%s' or content = '%s'". Quotes and SQL operators escape the string literals, allowing alteration of the query predicate and extraction of database data.

systemDebug interpolates the unauthenticated arg argument into 'ps {}'. helpers.run_cmd executes the resulting string through os.popen in core/helpers.py:9. Shell metacharacters in arg execute arbitrary commands with the application's privileges; neither difficulty mode sanitizes this argument.

importPaste places client-controlled scheme, host, port and path into an unquoted curl shell command executed by os.popen. Easy mode performs no filtering; hard mode removes only semicolons and ampersands. Pipes, newlines and command substitutions remain usable for unauthenticated arbitrary command execution.

After checking administrator credentials, systemDiagnostics executes the entire client-supplied cmd through os.popen. allowed_cmds accepts everything in easy mode and checks only string prefixes in hard mode. A value such as 'echo ok; id' passes the hard-mode check and executes additional arbitrary commands.

The unauthenticated uploadPaste mutation passes filename and content directly to save_file. open(WEB_UPLOADDIR + filename, 'w') permits ../ traversal and truncates existing files. Attackers can create or overwrite files outside pastes/, including application code or templates wherever filesystem permissions allow.

importPaste fetches an arbitrary client-selected scheme, host, port and path without destination restrictions. Unauthenticated callers can target loopback, private networks or metadata services accessible to the server. The fetched response is returned as result and persisted as paste content.

Every imported HTTPS paste is fetched using curl --insecure, disabling certificate and hostname verification. A network attacker can impersonate the selected HTTPS source and substitute content that the application returns and stores.

get_identity decodes JWTs with verify_signature=False and verify_exp=False. resolve_me trusts the resulting identity and places it in the authorization context. An attacker can fabricate an admin identity without a valid signature, retrieve the administrator record and expose its plaintext password; expired tokens also remain accepted.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: Password disclosure is authorized solely by info.context.json.get('identity') == 'admin'. This is the client-controlled HTTP JSON body. Sending a users query with an additional top-level identity value of admin exposes users' plaintext passwords without logging in or supplying any JWT.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: JWT_SECRET_KEY is the hardcoded string 'dvga'. The login mutation issues tokens using this publicly known signing key, allowing anyone with the source to generate correctly signed tokens. The preceding Flask SECRET_KEY assignment uses the same constant.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: Database initialization creates admin with password 'changeme' because random_password selects from a one-element list, and operator with 'password123'. Startup and /start_over reinstall these known credentials, which are accepted by login and the administrator diagnostics check.

CreateUser forwards user_data.password unchanged to User.create_user, which commits it directly to the users.password column. Login subsequently compares the submitted password directly against that column. Database access or password-field disclosure therefore reveals usable passwords rather than salted password hashes.

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password

extra.message: Login checks every supplied username/password pair without throttling, lockout or an attempt budget. systemDiagnostics likewise checks administrator credentials on every invocation. GraphQL aliases and enabled batching permit many guesses per request, and the cost table assigns neither operation a cost, enabling unrestricted password brute force.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: editPaste updates a paste selected only by the client-supplied id. No authentication, ownership or visibility check precedes the update. Any caller can overwrite another paste's title and content, including private and burn-after-read pastes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: deletePaste deletes and commits a paste selected solely by a client-controlled id. No authentication or ownership validation is performed, allowing unauthenticated callers to delete arbitrary public, private or burn-after-read pastes.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The paste resolver returns a record by client-supplied title or id with only burn=False filtering. It never checks public visibility or ownership. An unauthenticated caller can enumerate sequential IDs or known titles to retrieve private paste contents and associated metadata.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The unauthenticated pastes resolver defaults public to False and directly filters by the caller-selected visibility. There is no owner or authenticated-user restriction, so a basic pastes query lists private paste contents and metadata across owners.

search queries all pastes or filters only their titles, without authentication, ownership, public or burn restrictions. Attackers can retrieve private and burn-after-read content. Unlike readAndBurn, this route does not delete burn pastes, allowing repeated reads that defeat their one-time disclosure behavior.

OwnerObject exposes the Owner model's paste relationships without a filtering resolver. A caller can traverse paste.owner.pastes to retrieve other pastes belonging to that owner, including private and burn-after-read records. These relationship reads bypass the top-level burn filters and never consume burn pastes.

readAndBurn reads and deletes a burn paste using only its sequential integer id. No authenticated owner or unguessable access token is required. An attacker can enumerate IDs to steal another user's one-time content and destroy the intended recipient's access.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The paste subscription forwards every global_event unchanged. The after_insert listener publishes every new Paste, including private and burn-after-read entries, and /subscriptions requires no authentication. Any subscriber can receive their contents and metadata without ownership or visibility checks.

deleteAllPastes is publicly exposed as a GraphQL query and unconditionally executes Paste.query.delete() followed by commit. There is no authentication or administrative authorization, allowing any caller to erase every paste.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The unauthenticated /start_over endpoint invokes setup.py through helpers.initialize. setup.clean_up removes the upload directory and database, then recreates default data and credentials. Any caller can destroy all stored pastes, users and audit history and reset the server's security mode.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Before every HTTP request, an unauthenticated X-DVGA-MODE header can persistently switch the entire server to easy mode. /difficulty/easy provides the same capability. Attackers can disable depth, cost, introspection and query restrictions, and weaken command filtering, for themselves and all other clients.

/start_over performs a destructive reset on GET without a CSRF token or origin check; /difficulty/<level> likewise changes global security state on GET. An attacker-controlled page can induce browser navigation to these URLs, triggering changes through a victim's browser even when the attacker cannot directly reach the deployment.

The audits resolver returns every audit record without authentication or authorization. The /audit route at lines 426-429 exposes the same records. Stored GraphQL query text includes private paste contents and credentials missed by clean_query, allowing unauthenticated recovery of other callers' sensitive activity.

clean_query redacts only token and password literals with no whitespace between the colon and opening quote. Valid GraphQL such as password: "secret" or token: "value" is logged unchanged. Subscription queries are stored without calling clean_query at all. Passwords and bearer tokens therefore persist in audit records.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Stored paste title, content and User-Agent values are interpolated into HTML passed to jQuery append without escaping. The private gallery at lines 145-156 and subscription updates at lines 65-79 repeat this pattern. Attackers can create or edit a paste containing executable HTML that runs in other visitors' application origin.

The /graphiql error formatter attaches traceback.format_stack(), traceback.format_exc() and an absolute source filename to client-visible GraphQL errors. Malformed queries expose internal paths, stack frames and exception details, including validation errors occurring before resolver access checks.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: The unauthenticated systemUpdate resolver invokes simulate_load, which performs 201-501 iterations of time.sleep(0.1), occupying execution for approximately 20-50 seconds per call. Repeated requests, aliases or batches multiply this delay without an execution deadline, allowing denial of service.

get_depth counts only whitespace-delimited tokens equal to '{'. Valid compact GraphQL with braces attached to field names is assigned depth zero. This bypasses hard-mode MAX_DEPTH and permits deeply nested Paste.owner.pastes selections that repeatedly expand collections, exhausting processing time and response memory. Easy mode skips depth checks entirely.

Cost analysis extracts only whitespace-separated alphanumeric tokens rather than GraphQL fields. A valid query such as '{a:systemUpdate b:systemUpdate}' contributes no systemUpdate tokens and is assigned zero cost despite invoking two slow resolvers. Arbitrarily many aliases bypass hard-mode MAX_COST and amplify resource consumption.

Every resolver calling create_audit_entry iterates and inserts the entire HTTP batch into the audit table. A batch of N audited operations therefore creates N-squared audit rows, each containing query text, with repeated commits. /graphql enables batching without a batch-size ceiling, permitting disproportionate database, CPU and disk consumption.

importPaste runs curl without a transfer deadline or response-size limit, while helpers.run_cmd reads all stdout into memory. An unauthenticated attacker can choose a server that streams indefinitely or returns an enormous response, retaining a subprocess and exhausting memory; completed responses are additionally stored in the database.

Hard-mode introspection protection checks only __schema and is decorated with run_only_once, which marks the context before inspecting the first field. Placing __typename before __schema skips the later check. __type is also never rejected, allowing enumeration of schema fields despite the configured introspection restriction.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: In easy mode, GraphiQL execution is authorized solely by the unsigned client cookie env=graphiql:enable. Any caller can set this value to bypass 'GraphiQL Access Rejected' and execute operations through /graphiql without server-issued authorization.

cwe: CWE-565: Reliance on Cookies without Validation and Integrity Checking

extra.message: The hard-mode denylist recognizes only the exact normalized strings 'query{systemHealth}' and '{systemHealth}'. Naming the operation getPastes, aliasing systemHealth or adding another field bypasses the restriction and exposes server health data. processMiddleware also omits denylist checking for array batches.

cwe: CWE-184: Incomplete List of Disallowed Inputs

extra.message: Hard-mode operation restrictions trust the client-chosen operation name without binding it to permitted fields or operation types, and exempt unnamed operations entirely. For example, 'query getPastes { deleteAllPastes }' passes the allowlist while invoking bulk deletion. Renaming or omitting an operation name bypasses the intended restriction.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision
